title: In this world, every promise grows a flower out of your skin.
formula: Rule as the hook (every promise grows a flower out of your skin; kept = bloom, broken = rot + stink) -> world tour (Linda's marathon sunflower, Dad's six-year sink tulip, the 'I'll call you' guy you smell across the mall) -> you: the town flake, 14 rotten flowers + a fly since ninth grade, so nobody believes you (wound + flaw + running bit) -> rival's perfect version (Derek, running for mayor: 1,000 perfect flowers; routine: every morning a new promise that blooms the second he says it) -> the break (he promises to bulldoze the park and Grandma's hives) -> plant (every summer you've watched where her bees go) -> your first promise in years (save the bees: a bud on your hand) -> doubter (Grandma: three Christmases) -> weird prep (all her bees in a shoebox) -> setback (99 %, your bud browning; the park laughs when you call him a fake) -> big test (bees land on every real flower except Derek's) -> hidden plan revealed mid-danger (bees never land on Derek) -> reversal: the rival's own habit (he PROMISES they're real: a real flower shoots out of his nose and rots on live TV) -> reveal (sweat, glue, 1,000 fakes slide off, 1,000 rotten ones underneath) -> running bit pays off (your fly leaves you for Derek) -> callback (you can smell him from across the mall) -> loop: fourteen rotten flowers, and one that blooms
loop: Lines 1-3: every promise grows a flower; break it and it rots (and yours are all rotten: 14). Last: 'Fourteen rotten flowers... and one that finally blooms.'

voiceNotes.grandma: Lily (ElevenLabs premade): warm, velvety British woman, the closest premade to a fond, teasing grandma
voiceNotes.derek: Callum (ElevenLabs premade): husky trickster, a slick candidate with something to hide

facts: Fiction: no sources needed. One rule, said in lines 1-3 and shown before it matters: every promise grows a flower out of the promiser's skin; kept = it blooms, broken = it rots and stinks.

Fallout of the same rule (not new rules): rotten flowers draw flies (your fly, Dad's ear); a promise that is already false rots the moment it is said (Derek's nose flower); bees visit real blooms only (planted: you watch Grandma's bees from her porch every summer; a bee snubs Derek on screen).
Derek's 1,000 blooms are glued-on fakes hiding 1,000 rotten real ones; the clue is that they bloom the second he promises (a real one only blooms once the promise is kept).
Numbers: 14 (your rotten flowers, the loop), 1,000 (Derek's), 10,000 bees, 99 % in the polls: story numbers.

lines.narration: In this world, every promise you make grows a *flower* out of your skin.
lines.scene: Cold open, a sunny small-town square: a man on a bench takes his date's hands and promises; POP, a green bud shoots out of his elbow. Around them everyone carries flowers growing from arms, shoulders, heads: a mail carrier with daisies up both arms, a kid with one sprout on his knee.
lines.camera: MCU on the couple, the bud pops on 'flower', quick pull-out to the square full of flowered people
lines.gag: A bud pops out of a man's elbow the instant he says 'I promise'

lines.narration: Keep it, and it *blooms*.
lines.scene: Macro: the elbow bud unfurls into a big red flower, petals opening in a burst, pollen sparkling in the sun.
lines.camera: Macro push-in, the bloom opens on 'blooms'
lines.gag: The bud bursts open like a party popper

lines.narration: Break it, and it rots and *stinks*.
lines.scene: Same framing, match cut: the flower droops brown, petals fall, flies circle, green stink lines rise; a passing jogger gags and veers away.
lines.camera: Same macro (match cut), then a hard cut to the jogger's disgusted face
lines.gag: Flies circle the rotten flower and a jogger gags mid-stride

lines.narration: You see, Linda next door ran the marathon she promised: a sunflower on her *knee*.
lines.scene: Linda (headband, running vest with a race number, finisher medal) jogs past your fence, a giant sunflower blooming from her knee, bobbing with every stride.
lines.camera: Tracking her jog in profile
lines.gag: The sunflower on her knee bounces like a bobblehead

lines.narration: Dad's sink promise? Six years old. Dead tulip, on his *ear*.
lines.spoken: Dad's sink promise? SIX years old. Dead tulip, on his ear.
lines.scene: Kitchen: Dad reads the paper beside a sink with a bucket under the dripping tap; a shrivelled brown tulip hangs off his ear, a fly circling it. He waves the fly off without looking up.
lines.camera: MS on Dad and the bucket, quick push to the tulip on 'ear'
lines.onScreenText: Sticky note on the tap: FIX ME
lines.gag: The bucket overflows while Dad waves off the fly

lines.narration: And the guy who said "I'll call you"? You can smell him from across the *mall*.
lines.scene: A mall: far down the walkway a guy scrolls his phone, a rotten rose on his shoulder; a green stink cloud drifts the length of the mall, shoppers fan their noses, a dog faints.
lines.camera: Long telephoto down the mall, the cloud rolling toward the lens on 'mall'
lines.gag: The stink cloud rolls the whole length of the mall; a dog faints

lines.narration: And you? Fourteen rotten flowers, and a fly that's followed you since ninth *grade*.
lines.scene: You on Grandma's porch steps: fourteen droopy brown flowers poke out of your hoodie sleeves, collar and hood; one fat fly orbits your head like a tiny moon. You give it a tired look.
lines.camera: Hard cut to an MS of you, push to the fly on 'grade'
lines.gag: Your fly orbits your head like a pet

lines.narration: Most of them are from "I'll be there in five *minutes*."
lines.scene: Flashback inserts, same pose three times: you in bed under the covers texting 'omw 5 min', and each time a brown flower pops out of your arm.
lines.camera: Three hard cuts on the same bed framing (match cuts), the phone screen readable
lines.gag: You text 'omw 5 min' from under the covers, three times

lines.narration: So nobody in town believes a word you *say*.
lines.scene: The square: you say something to a neighbour; she glances at your rotten flowers, holds her nose and walks off; a shop owner flips his sign to CLOSED as you pass.
lines.camera: MS two-shot, then a quick reframe to the sign
lines.gag: A shopkeeper flips his sign to CLOSED as you walk by

lines.narration: Then there's Derek: running for mayor, a thousand perfect flowers, like a walking wedding *cake*.
lines.spoken: Then there's Derek: running for mayor, a THOUSAND perfect flowers, like a walking wedding cake.
lines.scene: The town park: Derek steps out of a shiny campaign van, covered head to toe in perfect pink and white blooms, teeth gleaming, a DEREK FOR MAYOR banner behind him. He spritzes himself with a perfume bottle.
lines.camera: Low angle tilt up Derek from his flowered shoes to his grin
lines.gag: Derek is so covered in flowers he looks like a three-tier wedding cake

lines.narration: Every morning, he promises the town something new: free pizza, a water park, no more *Mondays*.
lines.scene: Derek at a podium in the park, the crowd cheering; on each promise a fresh perfect bloom appears on his sleeve. Inserts: a pizza, a waterslide, a calendar with Monday torn out.
lines.camera: Hard cuts on each promise, MCU of Derek
lines.onScreenText: Calendar page with MONDAY torn out
lines.gag: A calendar where Monday is torn out

lines.narration: And they bloom the *second* he says them.
lines.scene: Macro on Derek's sleeve: he says 'promise' and a flower is just THERE, fully open, no bud. Behind his back his other hand tucks a glue tube into his pocket (planted, easy to miss). A bee buzzes up, sniffs one of his flowers, and zigzags away.
lines.camera: Macro on the sleeve, quick rack to his hidden hand
lines.gag: A bloom appears fully open with no bud, like a magic trick; a bee sniffs it and leaves

lines.narration: Then one Monday, he promises to bulldoze the park, and Grandma's *beehives*.
lines.scene: Derek points his plan board at the park's corner: Grandma's little white beehives under an apple tree; the board shows them replaced by a parking lot, a yellow bulldozer parked beside it.
lines.camera: Whip from Derek's pointing finger to the hives
lines.gag: The plan board draws the hives as a parking lot

lines.narration: You've spent every summer on her porch, watching where those bees *go*.
lines.scene: Grandma's porch, summer light: you with binoculars and a notebook full of bee doodles and arrows, a bee flying past your nose; Grandma knits beside you. The fly sits on your notebook.
lines.camera: MS of you on the porch, insert of the notebook page
lines.gag: You track bees with binoculars like a spy

lines.narration: So, for the first time in years, you promise to save them, and a bud pops out of your *hand*.
lines.spoken: So, for the first time in YEARS, you promise to save them, and a bud pops out of your hand.
lines.scene: At the hives: you take Grandma's hands; a tiny green bud pops out of the back of your hand, fresh and green among your rotten flowers. Your fly lands on it and you shoo it off.
lines.camera: Two-shot, then macro on your hand as the bud pops on 'hand'
lines.gag: One green bud among fourteen brown ones

lines.narration: "Sweetie, you promised to visit at Christmas. Three *Christmases* ago."
lines.speaker: grandma
lines.scene: Grandma (beekeeper hat, veil pushed up, cardigan) taps one of your rotten flowers; it drops a petal. On her shelf, a photo of an empty chair at a Christmas table.
lines.camera: MCU on Grandma, insert of the petal falling on 'Christmases'
lines.gag: Your rotten Christmas flower drops a petal when she taps it

lines.narration: You borrow every bee she owns. In a *shoebox*.
lines.spoken: You borrow every bee she owns. In a SHOEBOX.
lines.scene: Grandma's shed: you hold a sneaker shoebox wrapped in rubber bands, the lid bulging and buzzing; a few bees peek out of the air holes.
lines.camera: Push-in on the bulging, buzzing shoebox
lines.onScreenText: Sticker on the box: 10,000 BEES - DO NOT SHAKE
lines.gag: The shoebox lid hops up and down from 10,000 bees

lines.narration: But by Friday, Derek's at 99 percent, and your new bud is turning *brown*.
lines.spoken: But by Friday, Derek's at ninety-nine percent, and your new bud is turning brown.
lines.scene: Night, Grandma's kitchen: the TV shows a poll bar, DEREK 99 %; you stare at your hand, the bud's edges going brown. Blue night outside, warm lamp inside.
lines.camera: Over the TV to your face, then macro on the browning bud
lines.gag: Your fly lands beside the bud like it's waiting

lines.narration: At the debate, you shout "He's a fake!", and the whole park laughs at the *flake*.
lines.scene: Bright morning, the park: a debate stage, a crowd on folding chairs, news cameras. You stand up in the front row and point at Derek; the crowd roars with laughter, pointing at your rotten flowers; Derek smirks at the podium.
lines.camera: Wide of the stage, cut to you standing, then the laughing crowd
lines.gag: The whole crowd holds its nose and laughs at you at once

lines.narration: So you lift the *lid*.
lines.scene: Close on the shoebox in your lap; you snap the rubber bands and slowly lift the lid; one bee climbs out first and looks around.
lines.camera: Macro on the lid lifting
lines.gag: A single bee climbs out first, like a scout

lines.narration: Ten thousand bees pour out, onto every real flower in the *park*.
lines.spoken: Ten thousand bees POUR out, onto every real flower in the park.
lines.scene: A golden cloud of bees erupts from the box and sweeps over the crowd. Nobody gets stung: people giggle.
lines.camera: Ride with the swarm over the crowd (object POV), sweeping toward the stage
lines.gag: The laughing stops mid-laugh as the cloud rises

lines.narration: Linda's knee. The mailman's elbow. Grandma's *roses*.
lines.scene: Three quick inserts: bees cover Linda's knee sunflower like a fuzzy blanket; the mail carrier's daisies; Grandma's roses at the back, Grandma beaming. Your rotten flowers and Dad's tulip get skipped.
lines.camera: Three hard cuts, each a quick push
lines.gag: Bees wear Linda's sunflower like a fuzzy hat

lines.narration: Every flower... except *Derek's*.
lines.scene: The swarm hits the stage, splits around Derek like water round a rock and leaves him alone in a ring of empty air. Every head in the crowd turns to him.
lines.camera: Wide on the stage as the swarm parts, then a slow push on Derek's frozen grin
lines.gag: The swarm parts around Derek like he's a rock in a river

lines.narration: You see, all summer you've watched those bees, and they never, ever land on *Derek*.
lines.spoken: You see, all summer you've watched those bees, and they NEVER, ever land on Derek.
lines.scene: Insert: your porch notebook again, the page now readable: a bee doodle with an arrow bending away from a stick figure covered in flowers, 'DEREK - NEVER' circled three times. Cut back: your smug face in the front row.
lines.camera: Macro on the notebook page, hard cut to your smug MCU
lines.gag: The notebook page you scribbled all summer: DEREK - NEVER

lines.narration: "Pfft. Bees? I promise these flowers are *real*!"
lines.speaker: derek
lines.scene: Derek laughs too loudly into the microphone and slaps his flowered chest, sweat starting on his brow; a fake petal falls off.
lines.camera: MCU on Derek, low angle
lines.gag: He slaps his chest and a fake petal falls off

lines.narration: Pop! A new flower shoots out of his *nose*.
lines.scene: POP: a real green stem shoots out of the tip of Derek's nose and opens a small flower. He goes cross-eyed looking at it.
lines.camera: Hard cut to a CU, crash zoom on 'nose'
lines.gag: Derek goes cross-eyed at the flower on his nose

lines.narration: And it rots. Right there. On live *TV*.
lines.scene: The nose flower wilts brown in seconds, petals drop, flies arrive; a news camera's red LIVE light; the crowd gasps and pinches its nose.
lines.camera: Push on the rotting flower, cut to the news camera's LIVE light on 'TV'
lines.gag: The flower wilts like a time-lapse in two seconds flat

lines.narration: He sweats, so the glue melts, and a thousand flowers slide off like wet *stickers*.
lines.spoken: He sweats, so the glue melts, and a THOUSAND flowers slide off like wet stickers.
lines.scene: Sweat pours down Derek; his perfect flowers peel off in sheets, slide down his suit and pile at his feet; the glue tube falls out of his pocket.
lines.camera: Tilt down Derek as the flowers slide, following them to the pile
lines.gag: A thousand flowers peel off him in one sheet like a banana skin

lines.narration: Underneath? A thousand *rotten* ones.
lines.scene: Derek stands covered in brown rotten stumps, a fly cloud rising off him, green stink lines; the front row tips over backwards in their chairs.
lines.camera: Pull back fast to a wide as the stink wave hits the crowd
lines.gag: The whole front row falls backwards from the smell

lines.narration: Even your fly leaves you, for *Derek*.
lines.scene: Your fly lifts off your head, hesitates, and buzzes happily over to Derek to join his fly cloud. You watch it go and give a little wave.
lines.camera: Follow the fly from your MCU across to Derek
lines.gag: Your fly since ninth grade leaves you for Derek, and you wave goodbye

lines.narration: Derek loses. You can smell him from across the *mall*.
lines.scene: The same mall telephoto as line 6: now Derek at the far end with a shopping bag, a stink cloud twice as big rolling the length of the mall; the 'I'll call you' guy next to him holds his own nose.
lines.camera: Mirror of the line 6 mall telephoto, the cloud rolling toward the lens
lines.onScreenText: Newspaper on a bench: DEREK LOSES
lines.gag: Even the 'I'll call you' guy holds his nose next to Derek

lines.narration: Fourteen rotten flowers... and one that finally *blooms*.
lines.spoken: Fourteen rotten flowers... and ONE that finally blooms.
lines.scene: The park at the hives, golden light, the bees back home, Grandma beside you: on your hand the bud bursts open into a big rust-orange flower among your fourteen brown ones, and a bee lands on it. Your proud face, the hives blurred behind.
lines.camera: Macro on the bloom, rack to your face close-up on the last word
lines.gag: A bee lands on your flower, the first one that ever picked you
